standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the elementary etale neighbourhood (U, u) -> (S, s) and the open neighbourhood V of v = (t, u) in the base change which is finite over U with v the unique point over u, which is the construction at the heart of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of the relative assassin under base change
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, label divisors-lemma-base-change-relative-assassin, invoked at proof lines 4675 and 4687
standard_prerequisites.use: Transports a relative associated point of the module along the etale and finite base changes, first to the point zeta over xi and then to its image theta over U.

core_obligations: Make the morphism locally of finite type by shrinking, and apply the splitting lemma to T -> S and the point t mapping to s: this gives an elementary etale neighbourhood (U, u) -> (S, s) and an open V of the base change containing v = (t, u), finite over U, with v the unique point of V over u (proof lines 4653-4669).

Build an impurity over the base change: since V -> T is etale hence flat there is a specialisation v' leading to v mapping to t', the residue field extension kappa(t') inside kappa(v') is finite separable, and any point zeta over xi in the fibre of X over v' is again a relative associated point by base change of the relative assassin; because the closure of xi misses the fibre over t, the closure of zeta misses the fibre over v, so the triple over V is an impurity (proof lines 4670-4680).

Push the impurity down to U: let u' be the image of v' and theta the image of zeta in X_U; then theta specialises to u' and u' to u, the base change formula again makes theta a relative associated point over U, and since the morphism X_V -> X_U is finite the closure of theta is the image of the closure of zeta, so emptiness of the intersection with the fibre over v implies emptiness of the intersection of the closure of theta with the fibre over u; hence the triple over U is an impurity, as required (proof lines 4682-4695).
proof_roadmap: Split the quasi-finite morphism into a finite piece over an elementary etale neighbourhood (proof lines 4653-4669).
Lift the impurity to the base change by specialising along the etale morphism and using base change of the relative assassin (proof lines 4670-4680).
Push the impurity down to the etale neighbourhood using finiteness of the relevant morphism (proof lines 4682-4695).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a module has an impurity above a point with a morphism that is quasi-finite at the specialisation, then it already has an impurity presented by an elementary etale neighbourhood of that point (statement lines 4644-4651, tag 05J0). The proof is a real construction: it applies the lemma that splits off a finite part of a quasi-finite morphism at a point over an elementary etale neighbourhood, lifts the specialisation along the resulting etale morphism, transports the relative associated point along the base changes, and then pushes the impurity down from the base change to the etale neighbourhood using finiteness of the relevant morphism. The lifting and pushing of the impurity are the substance, so the claim is H2.
